page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS Graviton2 architecture. The instance provides 4 dedicated arm64 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores using the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. Each core has access to 64 KB of L1 data cache and 1.0 MB of L2 cache, supported by 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 8.0 GB, yielding a compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include integrated cryptography acceleration with hardware AES, while x86-specific vector extensions and simultaneous multithreading are absent.

Integrated storage consists of a dedicated 237 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume directly attached to the host, distinguishing the 'd' series from pure Elastic Block Store instances. Network connectivity is delivered via Nitro virtualization with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps. The instance does not include GPU acceleration hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, directing external network traffic through Elastic IP configurations or private network paths.

Benchmark outcomes show distinct performance trade-offs inherent to the ARM Neoverse-N1 processor. Stress-ng raw compute testing places both single-core (1519.58) and multi-core (6061.97) throughput in the middle 50% category, alongside average database operations in PassMark (2607.7) and average large-block memory read and write bandwidths. However, integer-heavy and decompression workloads reveal bottlenecks: single-core Geekbench (932.0), bzip3 decompression, and text processing fall into the bottom 10%, while Redis SET throughput (4.81 million ops/sec) and static web serving (5.01 GB/sec) score in the lower 25% bracket.

The qualitative trade-off of the c6gd.xlarge lies in its inclusion of high-speed local NVMe storage combined with power-efficient ARM dedicated cores. While raw single-thread instructions and floating-point computations lag behind higher-wattage x86 alternatives, the dedicated physical cores and local disk allow steady compute performance without hyperthread contention. This configuration is well suited for distributed application nodes, microservices, local caching layers, CI/CD build workers requiring temporary high-speed scratch space, and containerized web backends compatible with arm64.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gd.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Graviton2 platform using the arm64 ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture. Powered by the Nitro hypervisor, it features 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, clocked at 2.5 GHz, alongside 8.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per core). A key hardware inclusion is a local 237 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 1 Gbps baseline network capability. Benchmark evaluations position its stress-ng compute and large-block memory throughput within the middle 50%, although single-threaded Geekbench, decompression tasks, and small-model LLM generation fall in lower tiers. Lacking discrete GPUs, this instance provides cost-effective efficiency for arm64-compatible workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores and local high-speed scratch disk, such as CI/CD pipelines, containerized microservices, distributed data processing nodes, and intermediate caching layers.
